# Write navigable technical documentation

Explain systems according to reader needs while retaining their technical contracts.

[All skills](index.md) · [Collection overview](../../README.md) · [Research and inspiration](../../standards/framework-evidence.md)

## When to use it

Use for tutorials, how-to guides, references, architecture explanations and developer guides.

Example request:

> Explain the export flow so a marketing reader can find its purpose and an engineer can find the access contract.

Expected result: A purpose-led document with explained terms, visible constraints and routes to exact technical detail.

## A concrete example

This illustrative example starts from the source facts below.

**Source facts and constraints:** The export prepares a file of the member’s bookings. Access rules and an exact data contract are available to link.

**Before**

> The export orchestration materialises capability DTOs through the adapter.

**After**

> The export prepares a file of the member’s bookings. Link the access rules and data contract where engineers need the exact details.

## Install and use

Install this skill from the versioned collection in a supported Agent Skills environment:

```sh
npx skills add https://github.com/theGeekist/skills/tree/v1.7.0 --skill write-technical-documentation
```

Select the intended agent and installation scope when prompted. This CLI installation is separate from ChatGPT plugin registration and mobile availability. Client discovery and activation require their own verification.

Read the [complete skill instructions](../../skills/write-technical-documentation/SKILL.md) and [bundled purpose reference](../../skills/write-technical-documentation/references/technical-documentation.md) for the full conditions and exceptions.

## Practices behind this skill

Diátaxis informs the organisation of documentation around reader purposes, supported by Good Docs and relevant arc42 architecture views. Editorial checks preserve technical contracts while improving the explanations around them.

- [Diátaxis](https://diataxis.fr/start-here/)
